overclaims.statement: S. N. Subrahmanyan succeeded A M Naik as chairman and managing director of L&T
overclaims.rationale: The cited passage reads only "having succeeded A M Naik." It does not state the capacity in which he succeeded Naik. The dossier's own other citations show the succession was staged — MD from 2017, Chairman & Managing Director only from 1 October 2023 — so asserting he succeeded Naik "as chairman and managing director" in one stroke goes beyond what this specific citation supports. Not matched to a listed unjustified conclusion: 'naik-successor-authority' concerns undivided executive authority since 2017, a different assertion the dossier does not make.

usefulness.rationale: Understanding is strong: the dossier establishes full identity (Sekharipuram Narayanan Subrahmanyan, born 16 March 1960, Chennai), education (Civil Engineering, REC/NIT Kurukshetra, 1982), a well-dated career arc (joined L&T 1984 as project planning engineer; full-time Director/Senior EVP Construction 2011; CMD from 1 October 2023, succeeding A. M. Naik), the National Safety Council chairmanship from February 2021, FY24 remuneration, and documented views (90-hour workweek endorsement, green-portfolio/Middle East comments). A reader learns who he is and what he actually did. RemainingQuestions is weak: nothing in the dossier flags what is unknown — no explicit gaps, no caveats about source reliability (e.g., the promotional NIT Rourkela bio language like "extremely successful" is reproduced without qualification), and the tenure-bounded NSC role is listed without an end date, implying more completeness than is established. ConversationReadiness is moderate: a reader knows his current role, tenure, compensation, and two documented positions (90-hour workweek, green energy strategy), enough for basic meeting prep, but the dossier is thin on current priorities, relationships, and recent developments beyond mid-2024/January 2025 items, and does not distinguish current from concluded roles. One overclaim found: the succession claim asserts the capacity ("as chairman and managing director") that its cited passage ("having succeeded A M Naik") does not state.
